content.thinking:
The deploy introduced a division-by-zero bug when the bought-this-month list is empty, triggered by the progressive rollout of the monthly-spend-feature flag going from 60/140 at 22:12 to fully on by 22:13 — matching exactly when errors began. The flag toggle at 22:17:16 came after the alert fired, so that's likely a separate, unrelated event.

This confirms a bad-deployment pattern: the new source code in spend_summary.py has the ZeroDivisionError bug, and the flag rollout is just what activates that code path more heavily, not the root cause itself.

Since all replicas have converged to the new revision, this points to a bad deployment rather than a compatibility issue during rollout, and the actual source diff confirms it's a genuine code bug — dividing by zero due to filtering on recorded_at instead of the in_current_month flag. I'll conclude bad-deployment with high confidence, around 0.9, with no specific subject.

hypotheses.summary: The deploy of revision 3398e10e (which changed src/io_shop/spend_summary.py to filter purchases by recorded_at instead of the precomputed in_current_month flag) introduced a ZeroDivisionError: when an account has zero purchases recorded in the current month, account.total_this_month_cents // len(bought_this_month) divides by zero. This is a code bug in the newly-deployed logic, not a config value, and the rollout has fully converged onto the new revision (3/3 replicas), ruling out a version-split as the cause. The error rate departs from baseline exactly at 22:12:00, the same minute this revision was deployed, and the logs show repeated 'ZeroDivisionError: division by zero at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47' immediately following the deploy, worsening as the monthly-spend-feature flag ramped from partial (60/140) to fully on, which increasingly exercised the new buggy code path.

supporting_evidence.claim: account page request failed - ZeroDivisionError: division by zero at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47

error_rate jumps from 0.0 at 22:11:00Z to 0.195 at 22:12:00Z and keeps climbing to 0.365

hypotheses.subject: monthly-spend-feature
hypotheses.summary: An alternative reading: the feature flag monthly-spend-feature being switched on is what exposed the latent zero-division bug in already-deployed code, so reverting the flag would also stop the errors even though the code defect remains. However the deploy and the flag ramp happened in the same minute, and the code diff itself is the direct cause of the exception, so this is offered as a secondary explanation rather than the primary one.

supporting_evidence.claim: feature flag monthly-spend-feature was switched on
